blocks.text: 1. Transformer Architecture

blocks.alt: An input embedding goes through an encoder stack and decoder stack to an output

blocks.text: Multi-Head Attention, the final topic of the previous Attention Mechanism module, closed out coverage of every attention variant needed here. Transformer Architecture opens the Transformers module, an architecture built almost entirely around Multi-Head Attention, already covered.
It relies almost entirely on Multi-Head Attention, already covered, rather than the recurrent or convolutional approaches already covered throughout earlier modules in this course.
2. Recapping The Parallelization Advantage

This connects back to the parallelization benefit, already covered in Self-Attention. Self-Attention genuinely eliminated the sequential, step-by-step processing already covered throughout Vanilla RNN, LSTM, and GRU.
The Transformer genuinely builds an entire network around exploiting exactly that benefit, making parallelization a genuinely central design principle rather than just one nice side effect.
3. A Preview Of The Overall Structure

This connects back to the encoder-decoder structure, already covered throughout this course. The Transformer genuinely uses an encoder and a decoder, both covered in complete depth in the next two topics of this module.

Each is built from repeated, stacked layers of Attention and other components, a genuinely deliberate, repeated structure explored throughout the rest of this topic and the two that immediately follow it.

blocks.text: 4. No RNN Or CNN Involved

blocks.alt: RNN is compared against the Transformer, which uses pure attention

blocks.text: A genuinely important, distinctive architectural choice connects back to every Recurrent Neural Network architecture already covered throughout this course. The Transformer genuinely uses no recurrence and no convolution at all.

This is a genuinely dramatic departure from every architecture already covered in the RNN, LSTM & GRU, and CNN modules, relying instead entirely on Attention, already covered throughout the previous module.
5. A Preview Of Positional Encoding

blocks.alt: A token embedding adds to positional encoding to form the combined input

blocks.text: This connects back to order genuinely mattering, already covered in Sequence Data. Without recurrence, already covered in this topic, the Transformer genuinely needs another way to know each word's own position.

This is called positional encoding, covered in complete mathematical detail in the very next topic of this module, a genuinely necessary companion to the architecture already covered throughout this topic.
6. The Stacked Layers Concept

This connects back to Network Architecture, already covered in its own topic. The Transformer genuinely stacks many identical layers on top of each other, a genuinely deliberate, repeated structural pattern.
Each layer genuinely combines Multi-Head Attention, already covered, with a small feed-forward network, covered further in this module, forming a genuinely repeated, consistent building block.
7. A Preview Of Residual Connections

blocks.alt: A sublayer input feeds the sublayer and also adds directly to its output

blocks.text: This connects back to skip connections, already covered in ResNet. The Transformer genuinely uses residual connections around every single sublayer, directly reusing that earlier, proven idea.

This directly keeps this genuinely deep, stacked architecture, already covered in the previous section, genuinely trainable, echoing the exact same benefit already covered for ResNet's own genuinely deep design.

blocks.content: This reuse of skip connections, already covered in this topic, is a genuinely elegant example of an idea originally developed for Convolutional Neural Networks proving genuinely valuable in a completely different architectural context too.

blocks.text: 8. Why The Transformer Genuinely Replaced RNNs

blocks.alt: RNN processes sequentially while the Transformer processes in parallel

blocks.text: A genuinely important, real historical development connects back to Self-Attention's own long-range dependency handling and parallelization, both already covered. The Transformer genuinely combined both advantages into one unified, complete architecture.
This genuinely powerful combination, already covered in this section, is exactly why the Transformer largely superseded RNN-based approaches for many sequence tasks covered throughout this course.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing Why The Transformer Became Genuinely So Influential

blocks.alt: Needing parallelizable long-range modeling points toward the Transformer

blocks.text: This connects back to genuinely needing both long-range dependency handling and genuinely fast, parallel training. The Transformer, already covered in this topic, directly delivers both simultaneously.

This connects forward to Large Language Models, covered later in this course, built directly on this exact architecture. Understanding the Transformer now, already covered, is genuinely essential preparation.
10. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates the genuinely stacked structure of a small Transformer, showing several identical layers applied in sequence, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
sequence_length = 5
hidden_size = 8
num_layers = 3  # already covered as the stacked layers concept in this topic

def simplified_transformer_layer(x, rng):
    # a genuinely simplified stand-in combining Attention and a feed-forward step, already covered in this topic
    attention_output = x + rng.normal(scale=0.1, size=x.shape)  # already covered as a residual connection
    feed_forward_output = attention_output + rng.normal(scale=0.05, size=x.shape)  # another residual connection
    return feed_forward_output

hidden_representation = rng.normal(size=(sequence_length, hidden_size))
print(f"Input shape: {hidden_representation.shape}")

for layer_index in range(num_layers):
    hidden_representation = simplified_transformer_layer(hidden_representation, rng)
    print(f"After layer {layer_index + 1}: shape stays {hidden_representation.shape}, already covered as the stacked layers concept in this topic")

print("\nNotice the shape genuinely never changes across layers, already covered as this topic's own repeated, stacked structure")

blocks.content: Running this example shows the representation's own shape staying genuinely consistent across every stacked layer, exactly the repeated, uniform structure already covered as this topic's own defining architectural pattern.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: The Transformer is built almost entirely around Multi-Head Attention.
It builds an entire architecture around exploiting Self-Attention's own parallelization benefit.
It uses an encoder and a decoder, each built from repeated, stacked layers.
It uses no recurrence and no convolution at all, a dramatic departure from earlier architectures.
Without recurrence, it needs positional encoding to know each word's own position.
Each stacked layer combines Multi-Head Attention with a small feed-forward network.
It uses residual connections around every sublayer, reusing ResNet's own skip connection idea.
It combined long-range dependency handling and parallelization into one unified architecture.
